data.narrative:
NuScale Power operates in the nuclear energy sector, a space populated by 10 identifiable comparable companies—3 public and 7 private. The target raised over $600M and operates as a public entity. The private peer set includes Oklo, Helion, Valar Atomics, X-Energy, and Nano Nuclear Energy; public comparables trade under tickers OKLO, NNE, and SMR.

The peer-median valuation method proved inapplicable to this analysis. The nuclear energy sector contains only one company at NuScale's development stage, and adjacent-stage and similar-tier cohorts yielded insufficient data points (fewer than three required for statistical validity). Applying an all-sector median would introduce unacceptable bias given the narrow, capital-intensive characteristics of nuclear technology development. No other triangulation methods were documented as applicable to the available dataset.

Without executable valuation methods supported by the provided data, this analysis cannot responsibly output a valuation range. Analysts seeking a defensible estimate for NuScale would require either: expanded peer data spanning regulatory approval timelines and capex burn profiles; transaction comparables from the nuclear energy M&A market; or discounted cash flow modeling anchored to project-level economics and permitting milestones. The current comp universe, while relevant in sector taxonomy, lacks the density and stage-specificity necessary to triangulate a reliable multiple-based valuation.
